topSignals.title: Iran War "Islamabad MOU" (June 18): Strait of Hormuz ceasefire extended — European TTF peaked at >€60/MWh during crisis.
topSignals.text: The 2026 Iran war (US/Israeli operations vs. Iran from Feb 28) closed the Strait of Hormuz, disrupting 20% of global oil and ~20% of global LNG. European TTF gas prices nearly doubled to over €60/MWh by mid-March 2026; Asian LNG spot prices surged 140%; QatarEnergy declared force majeure. An initial April 8 ceasefire broke down (Iran reinstated blockade in mid-June citing US MOU breaches), but a new "Islamabad MOU" signed June 18 aims to extend the ceasefire 60 days and reopen Hormuz. Critical LCOE flag for INOCEL model: At €60/MWh TTF, SOFC fuel input cost ≈ €0.088–0.107/kWh (55–60% LHV) — vs. US Henry Hub $2.92/MMBtu where fuel input is $0.028–0.034/kWh. European NG-fueled SOFC was severely impaired at peak crisis. Post-MOU TTF recovery trajectory is now the #1 European LCOE variable. Storage remains critically low (~30% capacity mid-March vs. normal 60–70%). (Wikipedia: 2026 Iran war fuel crisis; Euronews: European gas prices; Al Jazeera: US-Iran MOU June 18; Wikipedia: 2026 Iran war ceasefire)

topSignals.title: BLM fast-tracks Green Chile pipeline for Project Jupiter (May 7 — first digest coverage)
topSignals.text: Bureau of Land Management granted expedited right-of-way for the ~18-mile, $60M Green Chile Natural Gas Pipeline using DOI emergency powers (14-day review vs. standard 1-year). Pipeline moves up to 400 MMcf/day from El Paso Natural Gas to the Bloom SOFC site in Doña Ana County, NM, for Oracle/OpenAI's Project Jupiter (2.45 GW Bloom SOFC). Partially resolves the gas supply uncertainty flagged in the June 9 digest. Remaining hurdles: (1) NM State Land Office denied state trust land rights; (2) FERC staff challenged Transwestern's application as incomplete; (3) NM environmental groups filed formal objections. Progress, not resolution. (Source NM: BLM fast-track; PGJ Online: BLM approves; Organ Mountain News)

topSignals.title: Bloom Energy risk flags intensify: $61M insider selling, 27× sales multiple, Morningstar "highly overvalued".
topSignals.text: Counter-signal to BE's ATH rally (+250% YTD, ~$329 as of June 20 close). Company insiders and directors liquidated >$61M in shares over the past 90 days. Morningstar flags stock "highly overvalued" at ~27× projected 2026 sales. Bernstein's MP initiation at $276 (June 16) sits ~16% below market. BMO Capital separately flagged that the Green Chile pipeline has not met FERC blanket certificate requirements — a potential Project Jupiter deployment bottleneck. No guidance revision expected by BMO, but the convergence of valuation pressure and infrastructure risk is a material counterweight heading into Q2 FY26 earnings (expected late July). (TradingKey: BE risks June 20; Investing.com: Bernstein initiation; Investing.com: BMO pipeline concerns)

items.text: Green Chile pipeline progress for Project Jupiter (see Top Signals #2): BLM fast-track is a partial win for Bloom's 2.45 GW Oracle deployment; remaining NM State Land Office and FERC hurdles still need resolution. Project costs: pipeline ~$60M ≈ $25/kW of installed SOFC capacity at 2.45 GW.
Confirmed SOFC pipeline (unchanged): Oracle 2.45 GW (NM), Project Jade/Google/Tallgrass 2.7 GW (WY), Nebius $2.6B, Brookfield $5B, AEP $2.65B, Equinix 100 MW+.

Germany EnEfG: July 1 deadline in 10 days. New DCs commissioning from July 1 must achieve PUE ≤1.2 at commissioning and ERF ≥10% (rising to 15% by 2027, 20% by 2028); 100% renewable electricity from January 1, 2027. SOFC CHP waste heat qualifies for ERF ≥10%. No new compliance guidance or amendments today. (Orrick: EnEfG draft amendment)
FERC RM26-4: RTOs have until ~mid-August 2026 to respond to Section 206 show-cause orders. Final tariff changes Q1 2027 earliest. SOFC BTM advantage intact during transition. (FERC.gov)

US Fed June 17 FOMC (first digest coverage): Rates held at 3.50–3.75% (12-0 vote). Dot plot hawkish: 2026 median rate revised to 3.8% (from 3.4% in March); 9 of 12 members back at least one hike. Fed Chair Warsh's first meeting. 2026 inflation revised up to 3.6% headline (from 2.7%), driven partly by Iran war energy prices. Higher rates increase WACC for SOFC project financing and data center investment. (CNBC: Fed June 17; StockTitan)

Iran war energy shock strengthens BTM SOFC case in Europe (see Top Signals #1): At peak TTF €60/MWh, European grid electricity costs surged sharply → on-site generation (including SOFC) with contracted or stored fuel gained structural appeal. Post-ceasefire, European energy markets face structural tightness: storage critically low, recovery will take months. Long-term argument for energy independence and on-site generation in Europe is reinforced. (Euronews: European gas prices; Wikipedia: 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis)
Quiet day on new nuclear SMR, CCGT, or grid-scale battery announcements since June 20.
